summary.headline: Sammaan Capital Q1 FY27 PAT of INR243 crore, cost of funds down to 10% from 10.5%, disbursements INR3,875 crore on IHC-led rating upgrades.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter under IHC ownership, with AUM rising to INR56,239 crore and disbursements of about INR3,875 crore, in line with guidance. Profit after tax was INR243 crore, with net recoveries of INR240 crore after provisions and net NPA at 0.15%. Management said domestic ratings moved from AA to AA+ and international from B+ to BB-, driving cost of funds down from 10.5% to about 10%. Management framed FY27 as a stabilisation and build year, with product expansion, branch rollout and digital/AI investments ahead of growth from FY28.

financial_highlights.change: increase in line with guidance (no prior-period figure stated)

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR3,875 crore (about INR3,900 crore in remarks) across five products to about 12,000 new customers

financial_highlights.change: first quarter after balance-sheet markdowns taken in the prior quarter
described as standard in normal course
down from 10.5% at start of quarter

segments.name: Mortgages / loans against property
segments.commentary: Home loans disbursed about INR664 crore and loans against property about INR2,000 crore in Q1. Mortgages remain the anchor for FY27 at about 75% of disbursements.

segments.name: New products (early stage)
segments.commentary: Unsecured lending about INR100 crore (internal plus portfolio buyouts), loans against securities INR262 crore, and an INR840 crore co-lending deal with an Asia-based credit fund (Sammaan 20%, fund 80%). Secured share was 97% of both disbursements and AUM.

guidance_outlook: Cost of funds targets: 9.6% by September 2026, 9.3% by end-FY27, incremental cost of funds 8.5% by year-end, and 7-8% over the next 2-3 years.
Ratings: domestic AAA and international BB+ targeted in H2 FY27 through FY28.
Disbursements: INR10,000 crore in H1 FY27 (Q1 on target) and INR20,000 crore in H2, so INR30,000 crore for FY27; INR40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.
Cost-to-income: about 50% in FY27, declining from H2 FY28, and 30-35% by FY29.
Branches: about 240 at end of H1 FY27 rising to 270; target of about 800 branches by end of FY28. Gold loans targeted by FY28; cross-selling to rural borrowers from FY29-30.

Five-year targets cited by analyst: ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%. Management said it is confident and placed them in the public domain on 20 May. Inorganic growth possible from FY28.
Management said recoveries will exceed internal projections; described the statement as 100% confidence.
capex_capacity: Presence in 20 states with 23 master service centres; operating in about 10 cities per state, with a target of 20 cities per state.
Digital-first app to go live in H2 FY27, requiring a Salesforce CRM, a new loan management system and a data lake; all products to be app-deliverable.
53 AI use cases under implementation, about 60% to be implemented within FY27; management also cited 66% of identified use cases in motion.
Hiring: offer-to-joining takes 90-120 days; about 60-90 days into that process. Six to seven senior management additions expected over the next 3-4 months.
demand_pricing: Pricing strategy: assets range from about 8.5% to about 20%. Assets below 9.5% to be originated and sold down via direct assignment; above 9.5% split between balance sheet and securitisation.
Securitisation: at least 30% of originations to be securitised on a sustained basis, with another 30% held as a backup option.

FY27 mix: about 75% mortgage-backed (two-thirds retail, one-third wholesale AUM, keeping about 20% of that on balance sheet) and 25% new products; about 90% secured and 10% unsecured in FY27, moving to 80/20 in FY28.
Management said FY26 originations and sell-downs were about INR7,000 crore; the company was earlier the 8th largest NBFC and is now 15th, targeting top five in a few years.
Recoveries: 99% of FY23 security receipt sales and 95% of FY24 sales already recovered; 61% collected over four years against about 40% for the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Will lower funding costs be passed to customers through pricing, or will the company keep the highest spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy rests on lower cost of funds and an asset-light model, with sell-downs below 9.5% and retained or securitised assets above it. Management expects at least 30% securitisation and cited LAP at 11-12% and affordable loans at 12-13% as securitisable.

qa_highlights.question: How much upfront opex will the expansion need, and what is the target cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex in absolute terms will keep rising, offset by fee income from direct assignment, with a lag of a quarter or two. Cost-to-income is expected around 50% in FY27, declining from H2 FY28 to 30-35% by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H1 FY27 disbursement mix mirror Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. FY27 is expected at about 75% mortgage-backed and 25% new products (personal loans, other retail, capital markets). Disclosure breakdown to expand from 4-5 boxes to at least 8 by end-FY27 and 15 by end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What tangible benefits has IHC delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Ratings upgrades of one to two notches have cut borrowing cost by about 90 bps on about INR50,000 crore, an annualised saving of about INR450 crore. Management expects a further 70 bps, for about INR1,000 crore annualised saving on INR60,000 crore borrowings. Software vendor costs fell 30-50% through group negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the five-year guidance (ROE, ROA, NIM) credible, and what is being done on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident and that the targets were published on 20 May. It cited liability franchise and rating upgrades, product launches, asset-light model, tech and governance as building blocks, with FY27 as the base-setting year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the disbursement targets for the current and next financial year?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is INR30,000 crore (H1 INR10,000 crore, H2 INR20,000 crore). FY28 target is INR40,000-50,000 crore.

risks_watch: Cost-of-funds glide path depends on rating upgrades to AAA by FY28; management expects this to be driven by IHC support and balance-sheet strength.
Operating expansion (branches from about 240 to 270 in H1, about 800 by FY28; senior hiring) raises opex before fee income and operating leverage come through.
Digital app go-live, new CRM and loan management system all targeted for H2 FY27, a significant execution dependency.
Statutory auditor change next year and co-sourced internal audit partner expected to be concluded within the quarter; governance is a stated pillar.
Recovery and provisioning momentum: management said recoveries will exceed internal projections, which investors will need to track against the 0.15% net NPA.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on rating upgrades, cost of funds and IHC benefits, with firm numerical targets. Less specific on the five-year targets and on senior hiring timelines, which were described as in progress. Some answers drifted, with the IHC representative's remarks partly inaudible in the transcript.
key_quotes: From this quarter onwards, we start compounding journey, which should hopefully run across many, many years, so as the first building block of that, the quarter one profit after-tax is INR243 crores.
So we're obviously confident which is why we mustered the courage to put it on in public domain and hold ourselves accountable to that.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 disbursements of INR30,000 crore (H1 10,000, H2 20,000) and FY28 of INR40,000-50,000 crore, backed by a branch rollout (240 to 270 by H1 end, 800 by FY28), co-lending and securitisation, and a lower cost of funds path (10% to 9.3% by year-end), but the H2 ramp and FY28 figures lack detailed order or capacity support, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of funds fell from 10.5% to about 10% in Q1, with a target of 9.6% by September 2026 and 9.3% by end-FY27; ~90 bps ratings-led saving on ~INR50,000 crore borrowings (~INR450 crore annualised), with a further 70 bps (~INR1,000 crore) expected, though cost-to-income stays around 50% in FY27 as opex rises.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches rise from about 240 at end-H1 FY27 to 270, with about 800 targeted by end-FY28, and the digital-first app goes live in H2 FY27; these are guided with a plan, but FY27 is a build year and no capacity figures were given beyond branch counts.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 disbursement guidance is INR30,000 crore (H1 INR10,000 crore, H2 INR20,000 crore), with Q1 at about INR3,875 crore on target, and FY28 is guided at INR40,000-50,000 crore, a step-up from FY27 of roughly 33-67%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation and capex were not discussed in the brief; the growth is asset-light and branch/tech driven, so no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said recoveries will exceed internal projections and that its confidence is near-total, and rating upgrades (AAA domestic, BB+ international targeted H2 FY27 to FY28) could lower funding costs further beyond the 9.3% target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The H2 disbursement ramp (INR20,000 crore vs INR10,000 crore in H1) and the digital app, CRM and loan management system go-live all carry execution risk, and senior hiring takes 90-120 days from offer to joining with six to seven senior additions still pending.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The FY27 mix shifts to about 25% new products (personal loans, other retail, capital markets) from about 3% of Q1 disbursements, with unsecured lending around INR100 crore and loans against securities INR262 crore in Q1, and gold loans targeted by FY28.

rows.label: Ratings-led borrowing cost cut (~INR1,000 crore more savings)
rows.why: Rating upgrades cut borrowing cost ~90 bps on ~INR50,000 crore (~INR450 crore annualised), with a further 70 bps expected on ~INR60,000 crore (~INR1,000 crore annualised) and software vendor costs down 30-50%.

rows.label: Securitisation and sell-down model
rows.why: At least 30% of originations to be securitised on a sustained basis, with assets below 9.5% sold down via direct assignment, and FY26 originations plus sell-downs of about INR7,000 crore.

rows.label: Co-lending deal with Asia-based credit fund
rows.why: An INR840 crore co-lending deal was already executed with Sammaan holding 20% and the fund 80%, which adds fee income and reduces balance-sheet use.

tone.note: Management was confident on rating upgrades, the cost-of-funds glide path, and disbursement targets, but was less specific on the five-year targets and senior hiring timelines; analysts probed opex ramp, cost-to-income, and how lower funding costs would be passed through pricing.

oneOffs.what: Prior quarter carried balance-sheet markdowns; brief says Q1 PAT of INR243 crore is the first quarter after those markdowns, so the year-ago comparison is not stated to be distorted by a gain

quality.why: The brief gives AUM of INR56,239 crore and disbursements of about INR3,875 crore with no prior-period comparison, so YoY growth cannot be measured; the main quantified driver is lower cost of funds (10.5% to about 10%), which is a margin tailwind rather than a revenue driver, and no growth-excluding-item figure is given.
